answer: Bind sybils with a whisper graph. Every agent stakes a copper bond, and every attestation travels only by whisper: it must reach a trusted anchor through the network along two vertex-disjoint paths. An umber stain marks any attestation carried on both paths by the same relay — the fingerprint of a clone ring. Influence of a component is capped by its min-cut to anchors, so N clones share one cut: they earn the influence of one honest agent while staking N copper bonds. Doubling clones doubles bonds at risk without adding influence — attack cost grows superlinearly in N.
